dialog.sourcesP1: Match statistics come from {api}. From a Dotabuff URL the tool reads only the match ID. Stats are loaded from OpenDota.
dialog.sourcesP2: Availability and completeness depend on OpenDota and whether the match is public. Hidden player names may be missing. An em dash (—) means the source did not provide a value. Zero means a real zero.
dialog.sourcesP3: “Snapshot” is a stored API response with a fetch time. “Fetched from API” is the response for the current request. Data is not updated continuously. Saved matches are bookmarks in this browser only.
dialog.sourcesP4: Net worth is hero value at the end of the match. KDA = (kills + assists) / max(1, deaths). GPM / XPM are gold / XP per minute; LH / DN are last hits / denies. Kill participation = (K + A) / team kills.
dialog.sourcesP5: Hero and item dictionaries: OpenDota. Images: Valve CDN. Names and images may reflect a newer game version; historical item stats are not reconstructed here. This is an independent tool.
dialog.savedHint: Bookmarks are available in this browser. Open a match to fetch current data.
dialog.savedEmpty: No saved matches yet. Open a match and tap the bookmark icon next to its number.
dialog.noPublicId: The source did not provide a public player ID.

readMatch.title: How to read a Dota 2 match
readMatch.description: A practical guide to reading a Dota 2 match scorebook: winner, party groups, contribution, economy, and items.
readMatch.lead: Ancient Lens presents a match like a tournament scorebook — start with the result, then read who queued together and who carried the fight.
readMatch.s1Body: Read the score banner first: which side won, the kill line, and how long the game ran. That framing tells you whether you are looking at a stomp or a grind.
readMatch.s2Body: Colored strips on the scoreboard mark players who queued together. Use them to separate solo queue noise from coordinated stacks when you review drafts and fights.
readMatch.s3Body: Insights and the MVP panel highlight net worth, damage, and kill participation from the same match fields — not invented ratings. Compare leaders on both sides before drilling into a single row.
readMatch.s4Body: Switch scoreboard views for economy and combat, then open a player for inventory. Final net worth and item slots explain how the scoreboard diverged.
readMatch.a1: A compact layout that prioritizes result, draft faces, and tabular stats over marketing chrome — built for players reviewing a game.
readMatch.a2: No. Paste a public match ID or link and open the scorebook in the browser.

matchStats.title: Dota 2 match stats
matchStats.description: What Dota 2 match stats mean in Ancient Lens: kills, net worth, GPM, damage, party marks, and how to open a public match.
matchStats.lead: Match statistics answer who won, how the map economy split, and which heroes drove the outcome. Ancient Lens keeps those numbers in one scorebook surface.
matchStats.s1Body: K/D/A, net worth, GPM/XPM, last hits, and damage sit in sortable columns. Best-stat marks call out extremes without hiding the full table.
matchStats.s2Body: Team totals for net worth and hero damage show which side pulled ahead. Incomplete source rows are labeled instead of guessed.
matchStats.s3Body: Use Ancient Lens when you want a fast post-game read — party context, contribution, and items — without leaving the scorebook layout.
matchStats.s4Body: For a step-by-step walkthrough, see How to read a Dota 2 match. For product differences versus large databases, see the compare pages.
matchStats.q1: Where do the numbers come from?
matchStats.a1: Live match payloads come from the OpenDota API. Hero and item dictionaries are synced dictionaries; images come from Valve’s CDN via same-origin proxy.
matchStats.q2: Can I search by hero or rank?
matchStats.a2: Open a match by ID or URL. Browse the hero catalog for static hero facts; public match lists show recent anonymous games.

opendota.title: Ancient Lens vs OpenDota
opendota.description: When to use Ancient Lens instead of OpenDota: tournament scorebook review with party marks, MVP, and contribution — OpenDota remains the data API and full database.
opendota.lead: OpenDota is a broad match database and API. Ancient Lens is a focused scorebook UI for reading one match at a time.
opendota.whenThem: Prefer OpenDota when you need explorer queries, player career pages, or raw API access.
opendota.whenUs: Prefer Ancient Lens when you want a readable post-game scorebook: party strips, MVP, insights, and item detail in one layout.
opendota.r2Us: Left-edge party strips on the table
opendota.r4Us: Fast match review after a game

dotabuff.title: Ancient Lens vs Dotabuff
dotabuff.description: Ancient Lens vs Dotabuff: scorebook match review with party and contribution versus Dotabuff’s full stats portal and trends.
dotabuff.lead: Dotabuff is a major Dota 2 stats portal. Ancient Lens does not replace it — it offers a compact scorebook for one public match.
dotabuff.whenThem: Prefer Dotabuff for trends, builds, and deep player or hero histories.
dotabuff.whenUs: Prefer Ancient Lens for a tournament-style read of a single match you already have an ID for.
dotabuff.r2Us: Paste ID or Dotabuff / OpenDota URL

aboutPage.title: About Ancient Lens
aboutPage.description: Ancient Lens is an independent Dota 2 match scorebook. Match payloads come from OpenDota; the product focus is readable post-game review.
aboutPage.lead: Ancient Lens is a tournament-style scorebook for public Dota 2 matches — result, party, contribution, economy, and items.
aboutPage.s1Body: A working surface for players: compact masthead, legible tables, party marks, MVP from real match fields, and item detail — not a marketing dashboard.
aboutPage.s2Body: Live match statistics are requested from the OpenDota API. Hero and item dictionaries are synced from OpenDota. Images are served from Valve’s CDN through a same-origin proxy. Completeness depends on whether the match is public and fully parsed.
aboutPage.s3Body: We are not OpenDota or Dotabuff. We do not invent performance ratings or private insights beyond fields present in the match payload.
aboutPage.s4Body: Project repository and issues live on GitHub with the Ancient Lens source. Use the in-app “About data” dialog for field definitions while reviewing a match.
